title: RandNLA Atlas
description: Normalized catalogue of the randomized numerical linear algebra results worth formalizing, what has been formalized where, and how results depend on one another. Four flat collections keyed by stable slug ids, so the same shape can live in a JSON file, a Prove2me mission series, or a shared document database with one collection per array. Version 0.2 adds search metadata (aliases, hypotheses, conclusion, uses_defs, variants, usage) so the atlas doubles as a fact catalogue for people and an index for prover agents; atlas/declarations.json is the generated per-declaration index that complements it.

areas.description: Topic taxonomy. A tree: top-level areas have parent = null.

priority.description: Captain's targeting priority for the area as a whole.

results.description: One entry per mathematical statement or definition. The unit a solver claims, a captain targets, and the viewer colours.

area.description: id of the most specific area

kind.description: application = an end-to-end algorithm guarantee that consumes the foundations; shown in the atlas as a consumer, not a target.

informal.description: One-paragraph statement in plain mathematics (KaTeX allowed).

status.description: proved: machine-checked and sorry-free somewhere listed in formalizations. scaffold: the formal statement exists in this library with a `sorry` proof (or is proved only modulo named scaffold lemmas); the statement is usable by downstream proofs. stated: a formal statement exists elsewhere and is open. assumed: consumed as an explicit hypothesis / Prop by a downstream formalization but not itself proved. planned: chosen as a target, no formal statement yet. candidate: identified, not committed.

label.description: Theorem/section label in that source, e.g. 'Thm 10.5'.

formalizations.description: Where (if anywhere) this result exists in Lean. Empty for planned/candidate.

usage.description: One sentence for a prover agent: what to pass and what you get, naming side conditions.

module.description: Lean module (import path), e.g. NLAlib.Matrix.SVD. Filled from declarations.json when absent.

depends_on.description: ids of results this one's proof consumes. Drives the dependency graph. Link status is derived: proved when both ends are proved; scaffold when both ends have a Lean statement in this library (one of them not yet proved); pending otherwise.

mathlib_prereqs.description: Mathlib declarations the formal statement or proof will lean on, and whether they exist today.

difficulty.description: 1 = routine once prerequisites exist, 5 = research-level formalization effort.

updated_by.description: Opaque user id, never a display name.

aliases.description: Alternative names people search for (theorem nicknames, source labels, informal names). Plain text.

hypotheses.description: The hypotheses of the statement, one per entry, with inline KaTeX math ($…$).

conclusion.description: The conclusion alone, with inline KaTeX math.

uses_defs.description: Fully qualified names of the library definitions the formal statement is (or would be) written with, e.g. NLAlib.frobSq. Tells an agent which API to state things in.

variants.description: ids of closely related results: other norm, scalar vs matrix, tail vs expectation, general vs specialised.

role.description: Why this source matters for the atlas (e.g. 'primary reference', 'cleanest proof').

libraries.description: Lean codebases where results live. Includes Mathlib itself.

ours.description: Maintained by this project (true) or external (false).

repo_dir.description: For libraries in this repository: the source directory, used by scripts/check_atlas.py to verify declarations exist.
